features.text: The patient is 26 years old.
The patient is undergoing full spectrum STD testing.
The patient is experiencing discomfort, a change in vaginal discharge, and an odor in the vaginal area.
The patient has soreness on the right side of the vaginal area.
The vaginal discharge is different in color and consistency from usual.
The soreness on the right side has been present for a few days.
The patient has not experienced fever, itching, or pain during urination or intercourse.
The patient has not had recent sexual activity with other partners.
The patient has been in a three-year relationship with her boyfriend.
The patient has not had any changes in menstrual cycle, including irregular bleeding or spotting.
The patient has not noticed any swelling or redness in the right vaginal area.
The patient has not experienced any recent trauma or irritation to the right side of the vaginal area.
The patient has not used any vaginal products like douches, creams, or contraceptives recently.
The patient has not had any recent sexual activity with new or multiple partners.
The vaginal discharge has a noticeable odor that is different from usual.
The discharge is more noticeable than usual but not yellow or green.
The patient has not experienced any itching or burning sensations with the discharge.
The physical examination showed no external lesions, and the cervix and vaginal walls were normal.
The patient has undergone swabs for STD testing and will provide a blood sample for syphilis, HIV, and hepatitis C.
The patient is aware that the test results will take time and that they will be contacted if anything comes back.
